args.text:
Committee Policy Actions
To back the Committee's dual-mandate goals, all members agreed to bump the target range for the federal funds rate up by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 per cent. They also reaffirmed the FOMC's policy of keeping ample reserves in the banking system. Members noted that the unemployment rate had hardly budged, while economic activity kept growing solidly and domestic spending held its own. Inflation was still running above the Committee's 2 per cent goal. The Committee made it plain it remained resolved to meet its dual-mandate goals, saying in its postmeeting statement that it "will deliver price stability." Members agreed the policy action would help get inflation back to the Committee's 2 per cent goal sooner.

Once the discussion had wrapped up, the Committee voted to direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to carry out transactions in the System Open Market Account under the domestic policy directive below, until told otherwise. The directive was for release at 2:00 p.m.:

"Effective September 17, 2026, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to:

Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-3/4 to 4 percent.

Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations at a rate of 4.0 percent.

Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 3.75 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day.

When appropriate, increase the System Open Market Account holdings of securities through purchases of Treasury bills and, if needed, other Treasury securities with remaining maturities of 3 years or less to maintain an ample level of reserves.

Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities. Reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency securities into Treasury bills."

The vote also gave the nod to the statement below for release at 2:00 p.m.:

"The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 12–0 vote:

The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.

Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.

Inflation remains elevated. Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability."

Voting for this action: Kevin Warsh, John C. Williams, Michael S. Barr, Michelle W. Bowman, Lisa D. Cook, Beth M. Hammack, Philip N. Jefferson, Neel Kashkari, Lorie K. Logan, Anna Paulson, Jerome H. Powell, and Christopher J. Waller.

Voting against this action: None.

In step with the Committee's decision to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 3-3/4 to 4 per cent, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to lift the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.90 per cent from September 17, 2026. The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System also voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point rise in the primary credit rate to 4.0 per cent from September 17, 2026.2

It was agreed the Committee's next meeting would be on Tuesday–Wednesday, October 27–28, 2026. The meeting adjourned at 10:15 a.m. on September 16, 2026.

Notation Vote
Through a notation vote completed on August 18, 2026, the Committee unanimously signed off on the minutes of its July 28–29, 2026 meeting.

document_config.guidance: Official prose (terms, policy, minutes, a job ad, an encyclopedia entry): keep every obligation, condition, name and number exact, and quoted documents verbatim. Aussify the connecting prose; no swearing at anyone.
document_config.embellishment_guidance: Dinkum: retell it in a genuine Aussie voice. Rephrase freely so each sentence sounds said, not translated; the odd opener, connective or tag-on where a talker would use one; the original's points in its order. Colour hangs off what's there: no new scenes, asides or punchlines. Where the genre keeps its form exact (a notice, a doc, official prose), the voice goes into everything around what's kept: say the connecting prose the way a local would explain it to a mate, at the level's weight, not in the original's officialese with a word or two swapped. What's kept includes the force of what it says: an obligation, a decision, a finding or a stated aim keeps its verb's weight ("we consider you responsible" isn't "we reckon"; "reaffirmed" isn't "doubled down"; a goal isn't "while they're at it").

result.scope: Issues: flagged phrases, swearing over the cap, US spelling and US words. Warnings: the guide's style rules and swearing density; fidelity to the original (length, names, numbers). Not checked: invented slang.
